title: Entity Matching using Decision Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.34626v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Entity matching is the task of deciding whether two records describe the same real-world entity. Current entity matching methods rely on pre-trained language models (PLMs) which require task specific fine-tuning or generative large language models (LLMs) which do not require task-specific fine-tuning but are slow and expensive at matching large record sets. Decision models are a new class of LLM-based models that return a probability for each predefined answer option rather than generate text. This paper investigates decision models as an alternative to generative LLMs and fine-tuned PLMs for entity matching. We evaluate six decision models in a zero-shot setting across eight benchmarks and compare their performance with that of the generative LLM GPT-6 Luna and the PLM-based matcher Ditto. Our experiments show that, without task-specific training data, the four strongest decision models achieve mean F1 scores close to that of GPT-6 Lu

translated_title: 基于决策模型的实体匹配
translated_abstract: 实体匹配是判断两条记录是否描述同一个现实世界实体的任务。当前的实体匹配方法依赖于需要针对特定任务进行微调的预训练语言模型（PLM），或者依赖于无需任务特定微调、但在匹配大规模记录集时速度慢且成本高的生成式大语言模型（LLM）。决策模型是一类新型的基于大语言模型的模型，它们为每个预定义的答案选项返回概率，而不是生成文本。本文研究了决策模型作为生成式大语言模型和微调预训练语言模型在实体匹配任务中的替代方案。我们在八个基准数据集上以零样本设置评估了六个决策模型，并将其性能与生成式大语言模型 GPT-6 Luna 以及基于预训练语言模型的匹配器 Ditto 进行了比较。我们的实验表明，在无需任务特定训练数据的情况下，四个最强的决策模型取得了接近 GPT-6 Luna 的平均 F1 分数。
tldr: 本文提出用决策模型作为实体匹配的新替代方案，证明其在零样本设置下无需任务特定训练数据即可取得接近生成式大语言模型的匹配性能。
